name: Embedded Payloads

evidence.rationale: File blocking mitigates embedded payloads by completely stripping high-risk file types at the perimeter, denying attackers the ability to deliver the initial malicious file or its nested, obfuscated components. Attackers frequently embed malicious scripts (e.g., .js, .vbs) inside legitimate document formats (e.g., PDFs, Word docs). By blocking macro-enabled or script-based file types, gateways prevent these malicious combinations from ever reaching the user's inbox
Attachment scanners and sandboxes can identify malicious payloads hidden within documents, scripts, executables, or other carrier files.
Host-based intrusion prevention capabilities can enforce behavioral rules that prevent execution of potentially obfuscated scripts containing embedded payloads.
